items.fullSentence: Je prends le petit-déjeuner à sept heures du matin.
items.sentenceTrans: I have breakfast at seven in the morning.

whyWrong.la matinée: That means 'the morning' (the time), not the meal.
whyWrong.le dîner: That means 'dinner' — dinner is not at seven in the MORNING.

items.fullSentence: Pour le goûter, elle mange une pomme.
items.sentenceTrans: For her snack, she eats an apple.

whyWrong.un pomme: pomme is feminine — une pomme, not un.
whyWrong.la pomme: la means 'the' specific apple; to eat one apple you need une.
whyWrong.de la pomme: That's partitive 'some apple'; a whole apple is counted with une.

items.fullSentence: Il mange de la salade et des tomates.

whyWrong.du salade: salade is feminine — de la, not du.
whyWrong.la salade: la means salad in general; here he eats 'some', so de la.
whyWrong.de le salade: de + le never stays split — and salade is feminine anyway: de la.

whyWrong.l'eau: That's 'the water'; to drink some, use de l'.
whyWrong.du eau: eau is feminine and starts with a vowel — it takes de l', not du.
whyWrong.de l'eaux: eau is singular here — eaux is the plural.

items.fullSentence: En France, on mange du fromage après le plat principal.
items.sentenceTrans: In France, people eat cheese after the main course.

whyWrong.de le fromage: de + le always contracts to du — 'de le' never exists in French.
whyWrong.de la fromage: fromage is masculine — du, not de la.
whyWrong.des fromages: des is plural 'cheeses'; the uncountable amount is du fromage.

items.fullSentence: Les Français mangent beaucoup de pain.
items.sentenceTrans: The French eat a lot of bread.

whyWrong.du pain: After beaucoup you use plain de, so no du here.
whyWrong.le pain: After beaucoup de you drop the article — beaucoup de pain.
whyWrong.pains: 'a lot of bread' here is mass — beaucoup de pain; beaucoup de pains would mean 'a lot of loaves'.

items.fullSentence: On va manger des pâtes ce soir.
items.sentenceTrans: We're going to eat pasta tonight.

whyWrong.de la pâte: la pâte (singular) means 'dough'; pasta is always plural, des pâtes.
whyWrong.les pâtes: les means the pasta in general; to eat 'some', use des.
whyWrong.du pâtes: du is masculine singular; pâtes is feminine plural — des pâtes.
